function.name: read_run_data
function.description: Read one section of the run summary in full (the context you were given is trimmed to fit). Sections: structure (cell lengths/angles of one unit cell, supercell, atom counts); symmetry (detected space group, tolerance ladder, Wyckoff orbits with displacement); pair_correlations (partial g(r) first peaks vs the average-structure neighbour distance); datasets (per-dataset Rwp).

function.name: find_gr_peaks
function.description: Analyse one partial g(r) (from the run's partial-PDF file): its peaks below r_max (position, approximate FWHM) and its first coordination shell, which does not depend on r_max — the window from onset to the first deep minimum (it holds the whole shell, split shells included), mean distance and spread from r²g(r), coordination numbers in both directions with their sensitivity to the cut, whether the shell is separated from the next, for a split shell joined across a deep trough its parts (CN, share, mean distance) and the long − short bond difference, the average structure's bond lengths for the pair against the window, and whether the pair's hard minimum-distance constraint cuts the distribution.

pair.description: Element pair, as labelled in the partials file.

r_max.description: List the peaks up to this r (Å). Default 6.

function.name: list_sites
function.description: List every reference site of the RMC configuration with its displacement statistics from a PCA of its displacement cloud: U_iso (Å²), principal RMS amplitudes (Å), anisotropy, Mardia and per-axis kurtosis, PC1 as [u v w], and a split site's static displacement (Å) with its sampling error.

element.description: Only the sites holding this element.

function.name: analyze_displacement_directions
function.description: Histogram the displacement directions of one site (site_ref, from list_sites) or of every atom of one element (element; "all" pools every atom) on the sphere, and test them: the peak direction (Cartesian and crystal [u v w], ± its cell's radius) with its calibrated significance, the whole-map test against isotropy, the +u/−u asymmetry, and the orientation-tensor anisotropy.

element.description: Pool every atom of this element instead of one site.

frequency.description: Sphere resolution (10ν²+2 cells). Default: chosen from the point count.

function.name: compute_bond_angles
function.description: Bond-angle distribution A–B–C with B the central atom (RMCProfile triplets): every pair of B neighbours, A within [r12_min, r12_max] Å of B and C within [r23_min, r23_max] Å (default: the A–B window). Returns the angle modes, mean ± sd, a 10° histogram, bond lengths and the B coordination, and for about six or four neighbours the split against an ideal octahedron or tetrahedron.

r23_min.description: B–C window minimum (Å); give both or neither.

window_confirmed.description: true only when the user chose or typed this window (in the question, or through ask_user). A window that cuts the coordination shell is refused unless it is set.

function.name: analyze_clusters
function.description: Shape of the finite clusters one element forms — the M4 tetrahedra of a lacunar spinel, dimers, trimers — with bonds in [r_min, r_max] Å in the average structure. Every cluster in the configuration is compared with a shuffle null in which each atom keeps its own site's displacements but takes them from a random other cluster: is there a distortion beyond independent atoms, which edge pattern (tetrahedra: E/T2 modes, trigonal vs one edge), along which lattice axis (<100>/<110>/<111>), and is the average cluster itself distorted.

element.description: Element whose atoms form the clusters.

function.name: analyze_modulations
function.description: Look for order that enlarges the unit cell — a superstructure the folded average structure cannot show (cell doubling as in low-temperature phases, octahedral tilts, charge-density waves). Fourier-transforms every site's displacements over the supercell's cell grid and compares the zone-boundary points (½,0,0)…(½,½,½) and the strongest modes with the configuration's own diffuse background (ratio to the median power, percentile). Optionally one element.

function.name: detect_symmetry
function.description: Run the space-group finder on the average structure (the folded reference sites) at a position tolerance in Å, as the Detected SG card does: group, number (only when it is certain), operations, and the Wyckoff orbits. Does not change the card.

tolerance_A.description: Position tolerance (Å); the card default is 0.2.

function.name: measure_symmetry_lowering
function.description: How far each average site sits from the position a higher-symmetry (parent) group puts it at: the size and direction of a coherent shift every copy of a site shares (a polar off-centring of the average structure). The parent is the group at parent_tolerance_A (default 0.2 Å, the Detected SG card's); the lower group is the one at tolerance_A (default 0.053 Å, just above the sampling noise floor). Each shift is in Å with its crystal [u v w], measured with the parent on the majority of the atoms, against the noise floor.

parent_tolerance_A.description: Tolerance of the parent group (Å). Default 0.2.

tolerance_A.description: Tolerance of the lower group (Å). Default 0.053.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the user ONE short clarifying question and wait for the answer. Only when the answer changes which analysis you run or its parameters (which coordination shell or r-window, which site or pair, which tolerance, which run or dataset) and neither the run context nor an analysis can settle it. Offer 2–4 short options, each with a one-line description (e.g. the window in Å), and your default.

label.description: A short choice, a few words.

description.description: Optional: one line saying what it means, e.g. "2.33–2.96 Å, both Ta–Se peaks".

options.description: The choices, the most likely first.

allow_other.description: Let the user type another answer. Default true.

default.description: The label of the option you would pick yourself.
